text:
lucy (NovaHealth): hi, we flipped on a client optimization to batch up short typing events into one call. since the rollout we've been getting intermittent 503s and a bunch of "slow" requests for tiny chat inputs. dashboard shows our quota fine. started ~09:12 PST. any ideas?

 tom (support): can you share org id, endpoint, and a couple request ids from failed calls? also is this mobile/web?

 lucy (NovaHealth): org nova-7, endpoint /v1/chat/completions. mobile (iOS + Android). sample ids: req_02A7L, req_02A7M. pattern: send 3-5 short user messages (20-60 tokens) coalesced into 1 request; often hit 503 or 200 but with 500-1200ms tail. sometimes the client retries and magnifies the issue.

 tom (support): adding jose from runtime and patrick from SRE to triage. @jose @patrick 

 jose (eng-runtime): thanks. quick hypothesis: continuous batching and our KV cache eviction policy interacting. if your batched messages create many distinct user prefixes, kvcache miss penalty + batch fill delays can push the request past service SLO and trigger upstream 503 or route-level throttles. do you have any client retry logic?

 lucy (NovaHealth): yes we had a naive immediate retry on 5xx with 3 attempts (no jitter). we assumed batching would reduce load.

 patrick (sre): infra logs for those req ids show a spike of concurrent short requests at 09:12:30, then a flurry of retries starting +40ms later. route token bucket shows momentary depletion and the service returned 503 (backend overload) for some. we also see kvcache miss rate jump for certain prefixes; cache size for our tenant is limited by policy and many ephemeral prefixes caused evictions.

 lucy (NovaHealth): can you paste the headers we saw? we captured one failure: 

```
HTTP/1.1 503 Service Unavailable
x-request-id: req_02A7M
x-service-status: degraded
x-rate-limit-limit: 120
x-rate-limit-remaining: 0
x-rate-limit-reset: 1882110600
content-type: application/json

{"error":"backend_overloaded","detail":"backend processing timeout"}
```
 lucy (NovaHealth): confusing because remaining=0 yet dashboard shows remaining tokens earlier in the minute.

 jose (eng-runtime): that header pattern matches per-route short-term burst budget exhaustion. dashboard per-minute aggregates can hide sub-minute spikes. also we have a protection that maps high retry fanout to temporary tougher surface-level throttles to protect cross-tenant latency.

 patrick (sre): we confirmed no org-level monthly quota hit. we saw a quick series of retries from multiple mobile clients within ~200ms which is classic retry amplification. the system treated that as a burst and returned 503/429 depending on whether backend queued the request.

 tom (support): TL;DR: client-side retries without jitter + coalescing -> increased tail latency due to batch wait + kvcache coldness -> retries amplify -> burst budget exhausted -> 503/429.

 lucy (NovaHealth): ok what should we change now? can't totally revert batching — it's key for mobile bandwidth.

 jose (eng-runtime): recommendation: client changes first (fastest):
- stop immediate retries on 5xx; add exponential backoff with jitter.
- when batching, add a small per-client stagger (random 0-30ms) so not all clients flush at same times.
- recognize 429/503 as signals to back off longer (e.g., initial backoff 200ms, double each attempt).

 jose (eng-runtime): server-side for short term (we can apply):
- temporarily raise per-route burst_capacity for nova-7 during your ramp window.
- enable kvcache prefix pre-warm for top-500 active prefixes if you can share list.
- lower max_batch_wait_ms slightly to avoid holding small batches too long (trades some efficiency for lower tail).

 tom (support): patrick can we give them a 90-minute burst top-up and lower max_batch_wait_ms to 25ms for their route?

 patrick (sre): yes we can. applying now and monitoring. will also flip on kvcache extra logging for nova-7 so we can advise more.

 deploy-bot: [2026-12-02T17:18:50Z] route-change applied for nova-7: burst_capacity:+150 until +90m; max_batch_wait_ms:25.

 lucy (NovaHealth): thanks — after the change we're already seeing fewer 503s. tail latency med->p95 improved from ~950ms to ~180-230ms. we'll roll the client retry patch out in the next 30m.

 jose (eng-runtime): follow-ups for best long-term behavior:
- instrument client to emit per-batch prefix key distribution and batch sizes so we can tune kvcache sizing or pre-warm patterns.
- if you expect many ephemeral prefixes, consider a tiny local LRU on client or group prefixes by tenant shard to reduce unique cache keys hitting backend.
- test different max_batch_wait_ms in staging to find your throughput vs latency sweet spot.

 tom (support): sample client retry pseudo: 
```
// typescript example
async function postWithRetries(req){
  for(let i=0;i<5;i++){
    const res = await fetch(req);
    if(res.ok) return res;
    if(res.status===429||res.status>=500){
      const base = 200;
      const jitter = Math.floor(Math.random()*100);
      const delay = Math.pow(2,i)*base + jitter;
      await sleep(delay);
      continue;
    }
    throw new Error('unhandled '+res.status);
  }
}
```

 tom (support): and server-side snippet we applied: 
```
route: /v1/chat/completions
max_batch_wait_ms: 25
burst_capacity: +150    # temporary top-up for nova-7
kvcache_pre_warm: enabled
```

 patrick (sre): note for internal runbook: add entry "perceived throttling: batching + kvcache evictions" with steps: ask for retry strategy, check kvcache miss rates, suggest burst top-up or warmup, consider per-route batch wait tuning.

 lucy (NovaHealth): will send prefix list and metrics after we roll client changes. thanks for the quick assist!

 tom (support): marking incident as mitigation applied; we will close after your 90m confirmation unless you ask us to keep monitoring. :white_check_mark:

 patrick (sre): internal note: follow-up item to evaluate default max_batch_wait_ms and kvcache eviction thresholds to reduce recurrence across tenants.
